sights.extract: Bingöl University (Turkish: Bingöl Üniversitesi) is a university located in Bingöl, Turkey. It was established in 2007.

sights.title: Hook Norton
sights.extract: Hook Norton is a village and civil parish in Oxfordshire, England. It lies 4+1⁄2 miles (7 km) northeast of Chipping Norton, close to the Cotswold Hills.

sights.title: Hook Norton Brewery
sights.description: Brewery based in Hook Norton, Oxfordshire, UK
sights.extract: Hook Norton Brewery is a regional brewery in Hook Norton, Oxfordshire, England, several miles outside the Cotswold Hills. Founded in 1849, the brewing plant is a traditional Victorian 'tower' brewery in which all the stages of the brewing process flow logically from floor to floor; mashing at the top, boiling in the mi

sights.title: Shutford
sights.extract: Shutford is a village and civil parish in the Cherwell district, in Oxfordshire, England, about 7.2 kilometres (4.5 mi) west of Banbury. The village is about 145 metres (476 ft) above sea level.

sights.title: Swalcliffe
sights.extract: Swalcliffe is a village and civil parish about 5 miles (8 km) west of Banbury in Oxfordshire. The parish is about 2+1⁄2 miles (4 km) long north–south and about 1 mile (1.6 km) east–west.

sights.title: Whichford
sights.extract: Whichford is a village and civil parish in Warwickshire, England, about 5 miles (8 km) southeast of Shipston-on-Stour. The parish adjoins the county boundary with Oxfordshire and the village is about 4+1⁄2 miles (7 km) north of the Oxfordshire town Chipping Norton.

sights.title: Hook Norton ironstone quarries (Brymbo)
sights.extract: The Hook Norton ironstone quarries (Brymbo) were ironstone quarries near Hook Norton in Oxfordshire, England. The quarries were in operation from 1899 to 1946, supplying ironstone to the Brymbo Steelworks in Wrexham and were served by the Brymbo Ironworks Railway, an extensive, 2 ft (610 mm) narrow gauge industrial rai

sights.title: Silbury Hill
sights.extract: Silbury Hill is a prehistoric artificial chalk mound near Avebury in the English county of Wiltshire. It is part of the Stonehenge, Avebury and Associated Sites UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sights.title: Avebury
sights.description: Neolithic henge monument in Wiltshire, England
sights.extract: Avebury () is a Neolithic henge monument containing three stone circles, around the village of Avebury in Wiltshire, in south-west England. One of the best-known prehistoric sites in Britain, it contains the largest megalithic stone circle in the world.

sights.title: West Kennet Long Barrow
sights.extract: The West Kennet Long Barrow, also known as South Long Barrow, is a chambered long barrow near the village of Avebury in the south-western English county of Wiltshire. Probably constructed in the thirty-seventh century BC, during Britain's Early Neolithic period.

sights.title: Windmill Hill, Avebury
sights.extract: Windmill Hill is a Neolithic causewayed enclosure in the English county of Wiltshire, part of the Avebury World Heritage Site, about 1 mile (2 km) northwest of Avebury. Enclosing an area of 21 acres (8.5 ha), it is the largest known causewayed enclosure in Britain.

sights.title: The Sanctuary
sights.extract: The Sanctuary was a stone and timber circle near the village of Avebury in the south-western English county of Wiltshire. Excavation has revealed the location of the 58 stone sockets and 62 post-holes.

sights.title: Kennet Avenue
sights.extract: Kennet Avenue or West Kennet Avenue is a prehistoric site in the English county of Wiltshire. It was originally an avenue of two parallel lines of stones 25m wide and 2.5km in length, which ran between the Neolithic sites of Avebury and The Sanctuary.

sights.title: Hill Head
sights.extract: Hill Head is a residential area and village on the coast of the Solent. It is located south of Stubbington, west of Lee-on-the-Solent and south east of Titchfield, in the borough of Fareham, Hampshire.

sights.title: Lee-on-the-Solent
sights.extract: Lee-on-the-Solent, often referred to as Lee-on-Solent, is a seaside district of the borough of Gosport in Hampshire, England, about five miles (8 km) west of Portsmouth. The area is located on the coast of the Solent.

sights.title: Fort Fareham
sights.extract: Fort Fareham is one of the Palmerston Forts, in Fareham, England. After the Gosport Advanced Line of Fort Brockhurst, Fort Elson, Fort Rowner, Fort Grange and Fort Gomer had been approved by the Royal Commission on the Defence of the United Kingdom a decision was made to build an outer line of three more forts two mile

sights.title: River Meon
sights.extract: The River Meon () is a chalk stream in Hampshire in the south of England. It rises at East Meon then flows 34 km (21 mi) in a generally southerly direction to empty into the Solent at Hill Head near Stubbington.

sights.title: Fort Brockhurst
sights.extract: Fort Brockhurst is one of the Palmerston Forts, in Gosport, England, and a scheduled monument. It is now an English Heritage property.

sights.title: Hovercraft Museum
sights.extract: The Hovercraft Museum is a museum located in Lee-on-the-Solent, Hampshire, England, run by a registered charity dedicated to hovercraft.

sights.title: Brittany
sights.extract: Brittany ( BRIT-ən-ee) is a peninsula, historical region and cultural area in the north-west of modern France, covering the western part of what was known as Armorica in Roman Gaul. It became an independent kingdom and then a duchy before being united with the Kingdom of France in 1532 as a province governed as a separ

sights.title: Brittany (administrative region)
sights.extract: Brittany (French: Bretagne [bʁətaɲ] ) is an administrative region of Metropolitan France, comprising the departments of Côtes-d'Armor, Finistère, Ille-et-Vilaine, and Morbihan. Its capital and largest city is Rennes.

sights.title: History of Brittany
sights.extract:
The history of Brittany may refer to the entire history of the Armorican peninsula or only to the creation and development of a specifically Brythonic culture and state in the Early Middle Ages and the subsequent history of that state.
Pre-Brythonic Armorica includes the ancient megalith cultures in the area and the Ce

sights.title: Pontivy
sights.description: Subprefecture and commune in Brittany, France
sights.extract: Pontivy (French pronunciation: [pɔ̃tivi]; Breton: Pondi) is a commune in the Morbihan department in Brittany in north-western France. It lies at the confluence of the river Blavet and the Canal de Nantes à Brest.

sights.title: Arrondissement of Pontivy
sights.extract: The arrondissement of Pontivy is an arrondissement of France in the Morbihan department in the Brittany region. It has 92 communes.

sights.title: Kerfourn
sights.extract: Kerfourn (French pronunciation: [kɛʁfuʁn]; Breton: Kerforn) is a commune in the Morbihan department of Brittany in north-western France. It is around 8 km east of Pontivy.

sights.title: Vendays-Montalivet
sights.extract: Vendays-Montalivet (French pronunciation: [vɑ̃dajs mɔ̃talivɛ]; Occitan: Vendais e Montalivet) is a commune in the Gironde department in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region in Southwestern France.

sights.title: Saint-Vivien-de-Médoc
sights.extract: Saint-Vivien-de-Médoc (French pronunciation: [sɛ̃ vivjɛ̃ d(ə) medɔk]; lit. 'St Vivien of Médoc'; Occitan: Sent Bebian de Medòc), or simply Saint-Vivien, is a rural commune in the Gironde department in Nouvelle-Aquitaine in southwestern France.

sights.title: Euronat (naturist resort)
sights.extract:
Euronat is a naturist holiday resort near the CHM Montalivet naturist resort, in Grayan-et-l'Hôpital, France.
After the success of CHM Montalivet, it was apparent that there was a need for even more capacity.

sights.title: Grayan-et-l'Hôpital
sights.extract: Grayan-et-l'Hôpital (French pronunciation: [gʁajɑ̃ e lopital]; Occitan: Graian e l'Espitau) is a commune in the Gironde department in southwestern France.

sights.title: Vensac
sights.extract: Vensac (French pronunciation: [vɛ̃sak]; Occitan: Vençac) is a commune in the Gironde department in Nouvelle-Aquitaine in southwestern France.

sights.title: CHM Montalivet
sights.description: World's first naturist holiday resort located in France
sights.extract: CHM Montalivet (CHM for "Centre Hélio-Marin", "center of sun and sea"), also known as CHM Monta, is the world's first naturist holiday resort, located south of Montalivet in Vendays-Montalivet, France. CHM Montalivet opened in 1950, and the International Naturist Federation (FNI/INF) was founded there in 1953.

sights.extract: Trogir (Croatian pronunciation: [ˈtro.ɡiːr]) is a historic town and harbour on the Adriatic coast in Split-Dalmatia County, Croatia, with a population of 10,107 (2021) and a total municipal population of 12,393 (2021). The historic part of the city is situated on a small island between the Croatian mainland and the isl

sights.title: Marjan, Split
sights.extract: Marjan (Croatian pronunciation: [mârjan]) is a hill on the peninsula of the city of Split, the second largest city of Croatia. It is covered in a dense Mediterranean pine forest and completely surrounded by the city and the sea, making it a unique sight.

sights.title: Čiovo
sights.description: Island off the coast of Croatia
sights.extract: Čiovo (pronounced [tʃîɔv̞ɔ]) is an island located off the Adriatic coast in Croatia with an area of 28.8 square kilometres (11.1 sq mi) (length 15.3 km (9.5 mi), width up to 3.5 km (2.2 mi)), population of 5,908 inhabitants (2011). Its highest peak is the 218 m Rudine.

sights.title: Kaštela
sights.extract: Kaštela (pronounced [kǎʃte̞la]) is a town and a suburb of Split in Dalmatia, Croatia. The town is an agglomeration of seven individual settlements which are administered as a single municipality, with populations individually ranging from 3,000 to 7,000 residents.

sights.description: Roman Catholic basilica in Trogir, Croatia

sights.title: Slatine
sights.extract: Slatine is a village on Čiovo, an island in Split-Dalmatia County, Croatia. It is a small fishing and tourist village situated on the northeastern side of the island Čiovo, only 8 km from Trogir.

sights.title: Ruhr pocket
sights.description: Battle on the Western Front in 1945
sights.extract: The Ruhr pocket was a battle of encirclement that took place in April 1945, on the Western Front near the end of World War II in Europe, in the Ruhr Area of Germany. Some 317,000 German troops were taken prisoner along with 24 generals.

sights.title: Unna
sights.extract:
Unna (German pronunciation: [ˈʊna] ) is a city of around 59,000 people in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, the seat of the Unna district.
The newly refurbished Unna station has trains to all major cities in North Rhine Westphalia including Dortmund, Cologne, Münster, Hamm, Düsseldorf and Wuppertal.

sights.title: 9ff
sights.extract: 9ff is a German car tuning company based in Dortmund. It was founded by Jan Fatthauer in 2001.

sights.title: Abbabach
sights.extract: Abbabach is a river in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, and a tributary of the Ruhr.

sights.title: Baarbach
sights.extract: Baarbach is a river of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, a left tributary of the Ruhr.

sights.title: River Douglas, Lancashire
sights.extract: The River Douglas, also known as the River Asland or Astland, flows through parts of Lancashire and Greater Manchester in North West England. It is a tributary of the River Ribble and has several tributaries, the major ones being the River Tawd and the River Yarrow.

sights.title: Kirkham, Lancashire
sights.extract: Kirkham aka Kirkam-in-Amounderness is a market town and civil parish in the Borough of Fylde in Lancashire, England, midway between Blackpool and Preston and adjacent to the town of Wesham. It owes its existence to Carr Hill upon which it was built and which was the location of a Roman fort.

sights.title: Warton, Fylde
sights.extract:
Warton is a village in the civil parish of Bryning-with-Warton, on the Fylde, in the Fylde district, in the county of Lancashire, England.
The village is 6 miles (10 km) west of Preston and 8 miles (13 km) south-east of Blackpool.

sights.title: Wrea Green
sights.extract: Wrea Green is a village in the Fylde borough of Lancashire, England. It lies about 2 miles (3.2 km) west of Kirkham.

sights.title: Freckleton
sights.extract: Freckleton is a village and civil parish on the Fylde coast in Lancashire, England, to the south of Kirkham and east of the seaside resort of Lytham St. Annes.

sights.title: Hesketh Bank
sights.extract: Hesketh Bank is a village in the West Lancashire district of Lancashire, England, 7 miles (11 km) north-east of Southport and 7 miles (11 km) south-west of Preston. sights.title: Avilés (comarca)
sights.extract: Avilés is one of 8 comarcas, administrative divisions of Asturias, which is a province and an autonomous community in Spain.

sights.title: Nalón (river)
sights.extract: The Nalón is a river in the autonomous community of Asturias, Spain. It is the longest river in Asturias, measuring 140.8 km (87.5 mi).

sights.title: Piedrasblancas
sights.extract: Piedrasblancas is the capital town of the municipality of Castrillón, in the province of Asturias, Spain. It is 5 km (3 mi) west of Avilés, 32 km (20 mi) west of Gijón, 40 km (25 mi) northwest of Oviedo and 6 km (4 mi) east of Asturias Airport.

sights.title: Battle of Shrewsbury
sights.extract: The Battle of Shrewsbury was fought on 21 July 1403, waged between an army led by the Lancastrian King Henry IV and a rebel army led by Henry "Harry Hotspur" Percy from Northumberland. The battle, the first in which English archers fought each other on English soil, reaffirmed the effectiveness of the longbow and ended

sights.title: Shawbury
sights.extract: Shawbury is a village and civil parish in  Shropshire, England. The village is 8 miles (13 km) northeast of Shrewsbury and 12 miles (19 km) northwest of Telford.

sights.title: RAF Shawbury
sights.description: Royal Air Force base in Shropshire, England
sights.extract: Royal Air Force Shawbury, otherwise known as RAF Shawbury, is a Royal Air Force station near the village of Shawbury in Shropshire in the West Midlands of England.

sights.title: Battlefield, Shropshire
sights.description: Village and suburb of the town of Shrewsbury in Shropshire, England
sights.extract: Battlefield is a village and suburb of the town of Shrewsbury in Shropshire, England. It is 3 miles (5 km) north of the town centre.

sights.title: Roden, Shropshire
sights.extract: Roden is a hamlet in the borough of Telford and Wrekin and ceremonial county of Shropshire, England, six miles northeast of Shrewsbury. The little River Roden flows past the village.

sights.title: Yorton
sights.extract: Yorton is a small village in Shropshire, England, north of the county town of Shrewsbury and south of the town of Wem.

sights.title: Astrakhan Kremlin
sights.extract: Astrakhan Kremlin (Russian: Астраханский кремль, romanized: Astrakhanskiy kreml) is a fortress in Astrakhan, Russia. It is located on a hill on an island in the Volga Delta, between the Volga, the Kutum, and the Tsarev.

sights.title: 2012 Astrakhan gas explosion
sights.extract: The 2012 Astrakhan gas explosion occurred on February 27, 2012, at an apartment building in the city of Astrakhan, Astrakhan Oblast, Russia. It was caused by a natural gas explosion.

sights.title: Astrakhan Governorate
sights.extract:
Astrakhan Governorate (Russian: Астраханская губерния, romanized: Astrakhanskaya guberniya) was an administrative-territorial unit (guberniya) of the Russian Empire, the Russian Republic, and the Russian SFSR, which existed from 1717 to 1929.
It was created from separating the southwestern part of Kazan Governorate by

sights.title: Port of Astrakhan
sights.extract: Astrakhan is a sea port in the city of Astrakhan in Astrakhan Oblast, Russia. The port is located in the Trusovsky District on the right shore of Volga river.

sights.title: Baku Mosque
sights.extract: Baku Mosque or Kriushi Mosque is a mosque built in 1907–1909 in Astrakhan. During the Soviet rule, the minaret of the mosque was destroyed, and in different years its building was used as a storehouse and cultural center.

sights.title: Astrakhan State Medical University
sights.extract: Astrakhan State Medical University (Russian: Астраханский государственный медицинский университет) is a higher education institution in Astrakhan, Astrakhan Oblast, Russia.

sights.title: Manipur University
sights.description: Public central university in Manipur, India
sights.extract: Manipur University (Meitei: Manipur Taibang Maheikol) is a public central university in Imphal, the capital of the north-eastern Indian state of Manipur. Its main campus stands at Canchipur, on the southern fringe of the city, where it occupies the site of the Langthabal Konung, a former royal palace.

sights.title: Shree Govindajee Temple
sights.extract: Shree Govindajee Temple (Meitei: ꯁ꯭ꯔꯤ ꯁ꯭ꯔꯤ ꯒꯣꯚꯤꯟꯗꯖꯤ ꯂꯥꯢꯁꯪ, romanized: Shri Shri Govindajee Laishang) is a Meitei Hindu temple, dedicated to Hindu deities Radha Krishna (Govindaji). It is the largest Vaishnava temple in Imphal district of Manipur, India.

sights.title: Zhangjiajie

sights.title: Tianmen Mountain
sights.extract: Tianmen Mountain (simplified Chinese: 天门山; traditional Chinese: 天門山; pinyin: Tiānmén Shān; lit. 'Heaven's Gate Mountain') is a mountain located within Tianmen Mountain National Park, Zhangjiajie, in the northwestern part of Hunan Province, China.

sights.description: Buddhist temple in Zhangjiajie, Hunan, China
sights.extract: Tianmenshan Temple (simplified Chinese: 天门山寺; traditional Chinese: 天門山寺; pinyin: Tiānménshān Sì) is a Buddhist temple located in Tianmen Mountain of Zhangjiajie, Hunan, China. The temple is built within grounds of some 20,000 square metres (220,000 sq ft) area.

sights.title: Puguang Temple (Zhangjiajie)
sights.description: Buddhist temple in Zhangjiajie, Hunan, China
sights.extract: Puguang Temple (Chinese: 普光寺; pinyin: Pǔguāng Sì) or Puguang Chan Temple (simplified Chinese: 普光禅寺; traditional Chinese: 普光禪寺; pinyin: Pǔguāng Chánsì) is a Buddhist temple located in Yongding District of Zhangjiajie, Hunan, China.

sights.title: Zhenhai Bridge
sights.extract: Zhenhai Bridge (Chinese: 镇海桥; pinyin: Zhènhǎi Qiáo) is a stone arch bridge in Tunxi District of Huangshan City, Anhui, China. The bridge spanned the Heng River for more than 400 years until being destroyed by floods in 2020.

sights.title: Tottori Sand Dunes
sights.extract: The Tottori Sand Dunes (鳥取砂丘, Tottori sakyū) are sand dunes located outside the city center of Tottori in Tottori Prefecture, Japan. With a length of 9 miles (14 km) and a width of less than 1.5 miles (2.4 km), it is the largest sand dune in Japan.

sights.title: Tottori (city)
sights.description: Prefecture capital and Core city in Chūgoku, Japan
sights.extract: Tottori (鳥取市, Tottori-shi; Japanese pronunciation: [tò̞t̚.tó̞.ɾʲí(.ɕì)]) is the capital and the largest city of Tottori Prefecture in the Chūgoku region of Japan. As of 30 November 2022, the city had an estimated population of 183,383 in 81,732 households and a population density of 240 persons per km2.

sights.title: Tottori University
sights.extract: National University Corporation Tottori University (国立大学法人鳥取大学, Tottori Daigaku), abbreviated to Toridai (鳥大), is a national university in Japan. The main campus is located in Koyamachō-Minami, Tottori City, Tottori Prefecture.

sights.title: Axis Bird Stadium
sights.extract: The Axis Bird Stadium (Axis バードスタジアム) is a 16,033-capacity multi-purpose stadium in Tottori, Tottori. The stadium is home to J3 League side Gainare Tottori.

sights.title: 1943 Tottori earthquake
sights.extract: The Tottori earthquake (鳥取地震, Tottori jishin) occurred in Tottori prefecture, Japan at 17:36 local time on September 10, 1943. Although the earthquake occurred during World War II, information about the disaster was not censored, and relief volunteers and supplies came from many parts of the Empire of Japan, including

sights.title: Tottori Tōshō-gū
sights.description: Shinto shrine in Tottori, Tottori Prefecture, Japan
sights.extract: The Tottori Tōshō-gū (鳥取東照宮) is a Shinto shrine located in the city of Tottori, Tottori Prefecture, Japan. Until 2011, it was called the Ōchidani Jinja (樗谿神社).

sights.title: Anamizu
sights.extract: Anamizu (穴水町, Anamizu-machi) is a town located in Hōsu District (formerly Fugeshi District), Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan. As of 30 September 2021, the town had an estimated population of 7,782 in 3,653 households, and a population density of 42 persons per km2.

sights.title: Cape Stolbchaty
sights.extract: Cape Stolbchaty (Russian: мыс Столбчатый, IPA: [mɨs ˈstoɫpt͡ɕɪtɨj], lit. 'Cape Columnar') is a geographic cape on the west shore of Kunashir Island, the southernmost of the Kuril Islands, in Sakhalin Oblast, Russia.

sights.title: Japanese cruiser Niitaka
sights.extract: Niitaka (新高) was the lead ship of the Niitaka-class protected cruisers of the Imperial Japanese Navy. She was the sister ship of the Tsushima.

sights.title: Ozyornaya (Sea of Okhotsk)
sights.description: River draining to Sea of Okhotsk in Russia
sights.extract: Ozyornaya (Russian: Озёрная, lit. 'Lake-river') is a river in the Kamchatka Krai of Russia. It originates in Lake Kurile and flows west to the Sea of Okhotsk.

sights.title: Wales, Alaska
sights.extract: Wales (Inupiaq: Kiŋigin, IPA: [kiŋiɣin]) is a city in the Nome Census Area, Alaska, United States. As of the 2020 census, Wales had a population of 168.

sights.title: Tin City, Alaska
sights.extract: Tin City (Inupiaq: Tupqaġruk) is an abandoned town except for a nearby minimally staffed radar station, in the Nome Census Area of the U.S. state of Alaska. It is situated at the mouth of Cape Creek, on the Bering Sea coast, 5 miles (8 km) southeast of Cape Prince of Wales on the Seward Peninsula.

sights.title: Fort Greely
sights.description: US Army anti-ballistic missile launch site
sights.extract: Fort Greely is a United States Army launch site for anti-ballistic missiles located about 100 miles (160 km) southeast of Fairbanks, Alaska. It is also the home of the Cold Regions Test Center (CRTC), as Fort Greely is one of the coldest areas in Alaska, and can accommodate cold, extreme-cold, and temperate-weather tes

sights.title: Juneau Empire
sights.extract: The Juneau Empire is a newspaper in Juneau, Alaska, United States. It publishes issues on Wednesdays and Saturdays.

sights.title: Eaglecrest Ski Area
sights.description: Ski area in Alaska, United States
sights.extract: Eaglecrest Ski Area is a public ski area on Douglas Island in the U.S. state of Alaska, across Gastineau Channel from Juneau. The area is owned and operated by Juneau's municipal government.

sights.title: Mendenhall Valley, Juneau
sights.description: Alaskan state capitol region geographical feature
sights.extract: The Mendenhall Valley (colloquially The Valley) [Lingít: Áakʼw Táak] is the drainage area of the Mendenhall River in the U.S. state of Alaska. The valley contains a series of neighborhoods, comprising the largest populated place within the corporate limits of the City and Borough of Juneau, Alaska's capital.

sights.title: Adair-Kennedy Memorial Park
sights.description: Sports complex in Juneau, Alaska, United States
sights.extract: Adair-Kennedy Memorial Park is a sports facility complex in Juneau, Alaska, and adjacent to Floyd Dryden Middle School.  It was named after Richard James Adair and Jimmy Earl Kennedy, two Juneau Police Department officers who died in the line of duty on April 17, 1979.

sights.title: Mendenhall Lake
sights.extract: Mendenhall Lake (Tlingit: Sit'.áa) is a proglacial lake in the Mendenhall Valley at the 1962 terminus of Mendenhall Glacier, three miles (4.8 km) north of the Juneau Airport in the Coast Mountains.  It is the source of the short Mendenhall River.

sights.title: Alaskan Brewing Company
sights.extract: Alaskan Brewing Company is a brewery in Juneau, Alaska, founded in 1986. It was the first brewery in Alaska after Prohibition.

sights.title: Wetaskiwin
sights.extract: Wetaskiwin ( wə-TAS-k(ə-)win) is a city in the province of Alberta, Canada. The city is 70 kilometres (43 mi) south of the provincial capital of Edmonton.

sights.title: Reynolds Museum
sights.extract: The Reynolds-Alberta Museum is an agricultural, industrial, and transportation museum in Wetaskiwin, Alberta, Canada. The museum is situated on an 89-hectare (220-acre) property containing the main museum building, an aviation display hangar, and its storage facility.

sights.title: Edmonton International Raceway
sights.extract: Edmonton International Raceway is a 0.250 mi (0.402 km), paved oval auto racing facility, outside Wetaskiwin, Alberta, Canada, approximately 72 kilometres (45 mi) south of Edmonton. The track is the first in Alberta to be sanctioned by NASCAR, and hosts races in the NASCAR Advance Auto Parts Weekly Series.

sights.title: Wetaskiwin Court House
sights.extract: Wetaskiwin Court House is a courthouse and National Historic Site of Canada located in the city of Wetaskiwin, Alberta.

sights.title: Bystrom, California
sights.extract: Bystrom is a census-designated place (CDP) in Stanislaus County, California, United States. The population was 3,957 at the 2020 census, down from 4,008 at the 2010 census.

sights.title: Ceres, California
sights.extract: Ceres is a city in Stanislaus County, California, United States. Its population was 49,302 at the 2020 U.S. census, up from 45,417 at the 2010 U.S. census.

sights.title: Empire, California
sights.extract: Empire is a census-designated place (CDP) in Stanislaus County, California, United States. The population was 4,202 at the 2020 census, up from 4,189 at the 2010 census.

sights.title: Modesto, California
sights.extract: Modesto ( mə-DESS-toh; Spanish pronunciation: [moˈðesto]; Spanish for "modest") is the county seat of and the largest city in Stanislaus County, California, United States. With a population of 218,069 according to 2022 U.S. Census Bureau estimates, it is the 19th-most populous city in California.

sights.title: Shackelford, California
sights.description: Neighbourhood in Stanislaus, California, United States
sights.extract: Shackelford is a southern neighbourhood of the city of Modesto in Stanislaus County, California, United States, which was officially annexed on June 1, 2012. The population was 3,371 at the 2010 census, down from 5,170 at the 2000 census.

sights.title: Modern Woodmen Field
sights.extract: Modern Woodmen Field is a 4,000-seat stadium in Modesto, California. It is primarily used for baseball as the home field of the Modesto Roadsters MLB Partner League team of the Pioneer League beginning in 2026 and was previously home to the Modesto Nuts Minor League Baseball team of the California League from 2005 to 2

sights.title: La Paz, Baja California Sur
sights.extract: La Paz (pronounced [la ˈpas] , English: "peace") is the capital and largest city of the Mexican state of Baja California Sur, with a population of 250,141 in the 2020 census. La Paz is located in La Paz Municipality, the fourth-largest municipality in Mexico by area (20,275 km2 (7,828 sq mi)), with a population of 292,

sights.title: El Centenario
sights.description: Place in Baja California Sur, Mexico
sights.extract: El Centenario is a small seaside town located in La Paz Municipality, Baja California Sur, Mexico, approximately 15 km west of La Paz, the capital city. El Centenario had a 2020 census population of 6,221 persons.

sights.title: Battle of La Paz
sights.description: Battle between the U.S. and Mexico as part of the Pacific Coast Campaign
sights.extract: The Battle of La Paz was an engagement of the Pacific Coast Campaign during the Mexican–American War. The belligerents were United States Army troops against Mexican militia, commanded by Mexican Army officers.

sights.title: Siege of La Paz
sights.extract: The siege of La Paz was a Mexican siege of their city of La Paz in Baja California Sur. Mexican militia forces attempted to destroy the United States Army garrison, occupying the peninsular town.

sights.title: Rockwood, Tennessee
sights.extract: Rockwood is a city in Roane County, Tennessee, United States. As of the 2020 census, Rockwood had a population of 5,444.

sights.title: Post Oak Springs Christian Church
sights.description: Historic church in Tennessee, United States
sights.extract: Post Oak Springs Christian Church is an independent, non-denominational Christian church in rural Roane County, Tennessee, associated with the Restoration Movement.  It is said to be the oldest Restoration Movement Christian Church in the American state of Tennessee, having been formed in 1812.

sights.title: Cardiff, Tennessee
sights.description: Company town in Tennessee, United States
sights.extract: Cardiff was a company town located in Roane County, Tennessee, United States. Established in the early 1890s by New England investors, the town was to house workers and managers for a large-scale mining operation that sought to utilize the abundant iron ore and coal resources along nearby Walden Ridge.

sights.title: Inwood, New York
sights.description: Hamlet and census-designated place in New York, United States
sights.extract: Inwood is a hamlet and census-designated place (CDP) in Nassau County, on Long Island, in New York, United States. It is considered part of Long Island's Five Towns area and is located within the Town of Hempstead.

sights.title: Rosedale, Queens
sights.extract: Rosedale is a neighborhood in New York City in the southeastern portion of the borough of Queens. The neighborhood, located along the southern part of Queens, borders Nassau County.

sights.title: Eastern Air Lines Flight 66
sights.extract: Eastern Air Lines Flight 66 was a regularly scheduled flight from New Orleans to New York City that crashed on June 24, 1975, when a Boeing 727-225 went on approach to New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport, killing 113 of the 124 people on board. The accident was determined to be caused by wind shear stemmin

sights.title: Springfield Gardens, Queens
sights.extract: Springfield Gardens is a neighborhood in the southeastern area of the New York City borough of Queens, bounded to the north by St. Albans, to the east by Laurelton and Rosedale, to the south by John F. Kennedy International Airport, and to the west by Farmers Boulevard.

sights.title: Eastern Air Lines Flight 512
sights.extract: Eastern Air Lines Flight 512 was a scheduled American domestic passenger flight operated by Eastern Air Lines from Charlotte Municipal Airport in Charlotte, North Carolina, to Idlewild Airport in New York City.  On November 30, 1962, while attempting to abort an attempted landing at its destination, the Douglas DC-7B o

sights.title: Bayswater Point State Park
sights.description: Public park in Queens, New York
sights.extract: Bayswater Point State Park is a 17-acre (0.069 km2) state park located on Jamaica Bay in Queens, New York. The park is located at the western end of Mott Avenue in Bayswater near Far Rockaway and is built on land that once housed the mansion and estate of banker Louis A. Heinsheimer.

sights.title: North Andover, Massachusetts
sights.extract: North Andover is a town in Essex County, Massachusetts, United States. At the 2020 census, the population was 30,915.

sights.title: Shawsheen River
sights.description: River in the U.S. state of Massachusetts
sights.extract: The Shawsheen River is a 26.7-mile-long (43.0 km) tributary of the Merrimack River in northeast Massachusetts. The name has had various spellings.

sights.title: Pemberton Mill
sights.description: Factory in Massachusetts, United States, which collapsed in 1860
sights.extract: The Pemberton Mill was a large textiles factory in Lawrence, Massachusetts, originally built in 1853. On January 10, 1860, at around 4:30 p.m., a section of the building suddenly collapsed, trapping several hundred workers underneath the rubble, in what has been called "the worst industrial accident in Massachusetts hi

sights.title: Weir Hill
sights.extract: Weir Hill Reservation (historically pronounced “wire hill”) is a 194-acre (0.79 km2) public park located in the town of North Andover, Massachusetts.  The Trustees of Reservations owns and maintains the property.

sights.title: Spicket River
sights.extract: The Spicket River is a 17.7-mile-long (28.5 km) river located in New Hampshire and Massachusetts in the United States. It is a left tributary of the Merrimack River, part of the Gulf of Maine watershed.

sights.title: Lawrence Heritage State Park
sights.description: State park in Massachusetts, United States
sights.extract: Lawrence Heritage State Park is a history-themed public recreation area dedicated to preserving the industrial heritage of Lawrence, Massachusetts. The state park comprises three separate units on or near the Merrimack River.

sights.title: Euclid, Ohio
sights.extract: Euclid is a city in Cuyahoga County, Ohio, United States. Located on the southern shore of Lake Erie, it is an inner ring suburb of Cleveland.

sights.title: Highland Heights, Ohio
sights.extract: Highland Heights is a city in Cuyahoga County, Ohio, United States. The city's population was 8,719 as of the 2020 census.

sights.title: Lyndhurst, Ohio
sights.extract: Lyndhurst is a city in Cuyahoga County, Ohio, United States, and an eastern suburb of Cleveland. The population was 14,050 at the 2020 census.

sights.title: Mayfield, Ohio
sights.extract: Mayfield, also known as Mayfield Village, is a village in eastern Cuyahoga County, Ohio, United States. A suburb of Cleveland, it is part of the Cleveland metropolitan area.

sights.title: Mayfield Heights, Ohio
sights.extract: Mayfield Heights is a city in Cuyahoga County, Ohio, United States. The population was 20,351 at the 2020 census.

sights.title: Richmond Heights, Ohio
sights.extract: Richmond Heights is a city in Cuyahoga County, Ohio, United States. The population was 10,801 at the 2020 census.

hotels.name: Comfort Inn Mayfield Heights Cleveland East

sights.title: International Seabed Authority
sights.description: Intergovernmental body to regulate mineral-related activities on the seabed
sights.extract: The International Seabed Authority (ISA; French: Autorité internationale des fonds marins) is a Kingston, Jamaica-based intergovernmental body of 171 member states plus the European Union. It was established under the 1982 UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and its 1994 Agreement on Implementation.

sights.title: Kingston, Jamaica
sights.description: Capital and chief port of Jamaica
sights.extract: Kingston is the capital and largest city of Jamaica, located on the southeastern coast of the island. It faces a natural harbour protected by the Palisadoes, a long sand spit which connects the town of Port Royal and Norman Manley International Airport to the rest of the island.

sights.title: Sabina Park
sights.extract: Sabina Park is a cricket ground in Kingston, Jamaica. It is the home of the Jamaica cricket team and is the only Test cricket ground in Jamaica.

sights.title: Lime Cay
sights.extract: Lime Cay is the main islet off the shore of Port Royal Cays, Jamaica. It is located in the northeast region of the reef.

sights.title: Parliament of Jamaica
sights.description: Legislative branch of the Jamaican government
sights.extract: The Parliament of Jamaica (Jamaican Patois: Paaliment a Jumieka) is the legislative branch of the government of Jamaica. Officially, they are known as the Houses of Parliament.

sights.title: Kingston Harbour
sights.extract: Kingston Harbour in Jamaica is the seventh-largest natural harbour in the world. It is an almost landlocked area of water approximately 16 kilometres (9.9 mi) long by 3.2 kilometres (2.0 mi) wide.

sights.title: Mare Harbour
sights.extract: Mare Harbour, known colloquially as East Cove Port, is a small settlement on East Falkland, on Choiseul Sound. It is mostly used as a port facility and depot for RAF Mount Pleasant, as well as a deepwater port used by the Royal Navy ships patrolling the South Atlantic and Antarctica, which means that the main harbour o

sights.title: Pleasant Peak
sights.extract: Pleasant Peak is a location on the Falkland Islands, East Falkland, two miles (3.2 km) north of RAF Mount Pleasant.

sights.title: 1982 British Army Gazelle friendly fire incident
sights.description: Helicopter downing in the Falklands War
sights.extract: On 6 June 1982, during the Falklands War, the British Royal Navy Type 42 destroyer HMS Cardiff engaged and destroyed a British Army Westland Gazelle helicopter, serial number XX377, in a friendly fire incident, killing all four occupants.
